newsitem.title: USA: Calif. bill seeks overhaul of state insurance post.
newsitem.headline: Calif. bill seeks overhaul of state insurance post.

text.p: A California Senator on Wednesday introduced a bill that would do away with statewide elections for insurance commissioner and instead require the governor to fill the post by appointment.
If approved by the state legislature and Republican Gov. Pete Wilson, the measure authored by Senator Quentin Kopp would appear on the state ballot as soon as next year.
"Electing the head of the Department of Insurance is an invitation to undue influence and even corruption," Kopp, an Independent, told a news conference.
The insurance commissioner's post had been filled by appointment before passage of California's Proposition 103 in 1988, which made the commissioner an elected position.
Kopp's bill was introduced a week after the Senate rejected his proposal to bar the insurance industry from contributing to the office of the insurance commissioner.
The two measures were prompted in part by a campaign finance controversy surrounding the current state insurance commissioner, Chuck Quackenbush.
Earlier this year, Quackenbush agreed to pay a $50,000 fine for alleged violations of state campaign contribution disclosure rules during his 1994 campaign.
Insurance company lobbyists expressed support for Kopp's new bill.

"We are pleased that Senator Kopp has addressed the politics inherent in an elected California Insurance Commissioner by offering a bill to make the position appointed," said Dan Dunmoyer, president of the Personal Insurance Federation of California.
